name: ARO-ALK7

lead: ARO-ALK7 is an experimental RNA interference drug aimed at the ALK7 gene, being tested for obesity in a first-in-human trial.
No results have been published, so its effects are unknown.

paras: RNAi drugs lower production of a chosen protein by silencing its gene; here the target is ALK7.
No safety data have been reported. The drug is investigational and not available by prescription.

trials.title: A First-In-Human Study of ARO-ALK7 in Adults With Obesity With and Without Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

lead: ARO-ALK7 is an investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapy directed at ALK7, a receptor involved in fat-cell signalling. It is being tested in adults with obesity, with and without type 2 diabetes. It is not approved for any use.[1]

The sole source of public information is a clinical trial registration: a Phase 1/2 first-in-human study (NCT06937203) that began on 9 May 2025, is recruiting, and plans to enroll 150 adults.[1] No results have been reported in the sources reviewed.
